page: Microsoft Azure D64pds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine powered by a Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The memory configuration consists of 256 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, featuring a 3780 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance supports Premium Storage.

In multi-core and memory-intensive benchmarks, the server demonstrates top-tier performance. It ranks in the top 10% for multi-core CPU stress tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and software compilation with Clang. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, achieving top-tier results in both small-block cached reads and large-block uncached read/write operations. Single-core performance, however, sits in the average tier, as seen in single-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests.

Given its ARM architecture, the server offers high resource density and power efficiency, translating to a cost-effective profile for highly parallelized workloads. The combination of 64 dedicated cores, high memory bandwidth, and a large local NVMe SSD makes it highly suitable for database operations, multi-threaded data processing, software compilation, and static web serving. It is less optimal for workloads requiring specialized GPU acceleration or single-threaded raw clock speed.
